metadata.title: US slows sale of Lukoil assets to pressure Russia in Ukraine peace talks

left: On Thursday, the U.S. Office of Foreign Assets Control will extend the February 28 deadline to April 1 for deals to be concluded, Reuters, Washington, February 26, 2026 reported.

The United States has slowed the sale to increase pressure on Russia in Ukraine peace negotiations, while U.S., Russian and Ukrainian officials have not made a breakthrough in Geneva, Abu Dhabi and Miami in recent weeks, with the next round planned for March.
Assets up for sale include oilfields, refineries and gas stations from Iraq to Finland, valued at $22 billion with OFAC extending deadlines three times amid interest from over a dozen bidders.

Senior U.S. officials escalated review of the sale, bringing in White House, Treasury and State staff, with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent more involved; the agencies declined comment on links to peace talks, and a sale could still conclude independently.

Earlier this month, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said his intelligence services told him that Russian envoy Kirill Dmitriev proposed a $12 trillion deal including Lukoil assets, which may complicate the sale.

right: The US Treasury extended the deadline for Russian company Lukoil to sell its foreign assets to April 1, replacing an earlier February deadline, and allows necessary transactions for sale negotiations while prohibiting fund transfers to accounts in Russia.
US officials are using the delay in Lukoil's asset sales as leverage in Ukraine peace talks involving US, Russian, and Ukrainian parties.

The sanctions forced Lukoil to sell a significant international portfolio, attracting bidders such as Carlyle Group and others, but the process is complicated by proposed economic deals involving Lukoil.
High-Level US officials are involved in managing the Lukoil asset sale process amid complex negotiations.

sources.text:
US extends deadline to April for Lukoil asset sale amid Russia sanctions pressure
Treasury Department replaces previous license; permits transactions related maintenance, wind-down of Lukoil’s international operations
ISTANBUL
The US Treasury Department said Thursday that it extended the deadline for Russian energy company Lukoil to sell foreign assets until April 1, issuing a new general license that supersedes a previous extension set to expire at the end of February.
The Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control issued a license authorizing transactions "ordinarily incident and necessary to the negotiation of and entry into contracts for the sale, disposition, or transfer of Lukoil International GmbH" and its affiliated entities through the beginnig of April.
Under the license, transactions related to the maintenance and wind-down of Lukoil's international operations are also permitted through the same date. But the license explicitly bars "the transfer of funds to any person or account located in the Russian Federation."
Any contracts entered into under the license remain contingent on receiving separate authorization from the Treasury Department before they can be executed, according to the agency.
Lukoil was sanctioned by Washington in October at the direction of US President Donald Trump, as part of broader efforts to squeeze Russia's energy revenues.
Lukoil is Russia's second-largest oil producer and a key target in Western efforts to reduce financial resources available for Moscow's military operations. The US frequently updates its sanctions licenses to manage the economic effect on global markets while maintaining pressure on the Kremlin.

sources.text:
U.S. Slows Down Lukoil Asset Sales Amid Ukraine Peace Talks
The U.S. has delayed Lukoil's international asset sales to pressure Russia in Ukraine peace negotiations, extending deadlines up to April 1. Lukoil's sales, vital due to U.S. sanctions, involve assets worth $22 billion. Major entities like ExxonMobil and Carlyle Group are interested buyers amid ongoing diplomatic discussions.
The United States has strategically delayed the sale of Russian oil giant Lukoil's international assets in a move to apply pressure on Russia amid stalled Ukraine peace talks, according to sources. The U.S. Office of Foreign Assets Control confirmed the deadline extension for concluding deals until April 1.
Despite negotiations in Geneva, Abu Dhabi, and Miami, no consensus has been reached among U.S., Russian, and Ukrainian officials regarding a peace settlement. The focal points of these discussions include U.S. sanctions on Russia's principal oil player, Rosneft, alongside Lukoil, highlighting the geopolitical complexities at play.
Lukoil's asset sale, driven by sanctions and valued at $22 billion, has attracted interest from firms like ExxonMobil and Carlyle Group. The White House and related U.S. departments have intensified their involvement, demonstrating the high stakes of these negotiations amidst the ongoing conflict.
(With inputs from agencies.)
